issues.description: The problem statement and UML require addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a reason String), but the provided solution implementation defines addGuestStudents with a single int parameter. This mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students about the expected method signature and prevents them from using the reason parameter described in the task.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's addGuestStudents method match the specification: change its signature to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and (optionally) store or log the reason as appropriate. Alternatively, if the reason parameter was not intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify a single-parameter addGuestStudents(int) so all artifacts agree. Ensure the template includes the matching signature to guide students.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a String reason) but the provided solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students with an associated reason) breaks the mapping between the exercise specification and the implementation and may confuse students about the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent with the problem statement: implement addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) in the template and solution. Update the implementation to accept and (if appropriate) record or log the reason, and adjust any callers or tests to use the two-parameter form.
